rationale: The pain is genuine and worsening as agentic coding tools proliferate — developers routinely fill terabyte drives with LLM-generated detritus and fear deleting anything. However, no willingness-to-pay signal exists: technical users in this space default to free/OSS tooling (dust, fdupes, custom shell scripts) and there's no paid substitute benchmarking our target price. The buyer is also underspecified — 'developers' spans students to staff engineers, and the segment that would actually pay for a polished cleanup tool vs. writing their own is narrow and not yet identified. Validate with a paid-tier landing page or a direct Reddit/HN poll before building anything.
solution_plan: WHAT: A Claude-powered CLI/web tool that scans a developer's working directory, classifies files as LLM-generated vs. project-critical, and produces a safe-delete manifest with dependency warnings. BUILD: The factory builds it as a Claude prompt pipeline (file-tree ingestion → classification → report) wrapped in a simple web form where users paste or upload a directory listing; payment via a one-time Stripe link ($9–$19) before the report is returned — no coding by Youval. SELL: Post a free demo version on r/LocalLLaMA, r/ClaudeAI, and the HN 'Show HN' thread; Youval approves each outreach batch before it goes out; conversion from free demo to paid full report is the validation gate. MAINTAIN: Submissions arrive via form, Claude processes them automatically, Stripe handles billing, and results are emailed — no per-customer human work; Youval's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches. CAVEAT: Until at least 10 paid conversions are confirmed, this is a validation experiment, not a product — the technical community's strong DIY culture makes paid conversion far from certain.
notes: buyer_clarity (5) and willingness_to_pay (3) both fall below build_gate floors (6 and 5 respectively). Stage is 'validate' both by total score (4.7 < 6.5 threshold) and gate logic. Primary risk: developers in this segment treat disk cleanup as a solved problem with free tools.
